out_items.name: Proper eating, tasting, drinking, or tobacco use

violations.title: Eating, Drinking, or Using Tobacco
violations.observation: Open drinking containers used or stored in a manner that may contaminate food, food contact surfaces or utensils. OBSERVED EMPLOYEE OPEN FOOD ON CUTTING BOARD IN KITCHEN.
violations.corrective_action: Food employees may have beverages in the kitchen areas as long as they are covered and consumed through a straw and stored in a manner that will prevent contamination to food, equipment, utensils, linens, and single service items. CDI: FOOD REMOVED FROM KITCHEN. PIC RE-EDUCATED.

violations.title: Separation of Raw Animal Foods Different Types
violations.observation: Different types of raw animal foods stored in such a manner that may cause cross contamination as follows: OBSERVED RAW CHICKEN STORED ON TOP OF RAW BEEF IN THE TWO-DOOR STANDING COOLER.
violations.corrective_action: Raw animal foods shall be sorted by their 'type' and cooking temperatures while in storage inside a refrigerator or freezer. For example, if using ONE shelving unit for storage of ONLY raw foods, the foods shall be sorted in this manner: 1) raw poultry (chicken, turkey, or duck) shall be stored on the BOTTOM shelf (165F cook temperature), 2) raw ground beef and ground pork shall be stored on the shelf above poultry (155F cook temperature), and 3) raw pork (chops, ribs), seafood, and shell eggs shall be stored on the top shelf above beef (145F cook temperature). CDI: RAW BEEF MOVED ABOVE RAW CHICKEN. PIC RE-EDUCATED ON CROSS CONTAMINATION AND STORING FOODS BY THEIR COOKING TEMPERATURES.

violations.title: Separation of Raw Animal and RTE Foods
violations.observation: Raw animal food storage, preparation, holding or display conducted in a manner that may cause cross contamination of ready-to-eat food as follows: OBSERVED RAW SHELLED EGG STORED OVER CUT CABBAGE IN THE TWO-DOOR PREP-TOP COOLER.
violations.corrective_action: Food shall be protected from cross contamination by separating raw animal foods like poultry, beef, pork, seafood, and eggs from cooked foods, ready-to- eat foods, washed produce, etc during storage, preparation, holding or display. Raw foods shall be stored on shelving units BELOW or SEPARATED from all cooked foods, commercially processed foods, washed produce, leftover foods, etc. CDI: RAW SHELL EGG MOVED TO THE B OTTOM SHELF. PIC RE-EDUCATED. Dolpan (Inspection Date: 07/22/2026) Page 2 of 4

violations.title: Hot Holding
violations.observation: The following food item(s) were observed hot holding at improper temperatures using a calibrated food temperature measuring device: OBSERVED IN STEAM TABLE: COOKED VEGETABLES IN STARCH AT 75F (30MIN), BLACK BEAN SAUCE AT 85F (30MIN)
violations.corrective_action: Time/temperature conrol for safety food shall be held hot at a temperature of 135F or above unless the permit holder is using 'time as the public health control' as specified under 3-501.19. CDI: PUT ON THE STOVE TO REHEAT TO 165F. PIC RE-EDUCATED ON HOT HOLDING TEMPERATURES AND PRACTICES.

violations.title: RTE TCS Food Prepared On Site, Date Marking
violations.observation: The following refrigerated, ready-to-eat, time/temperature control for safety food that is prepared on site is not used or discarded within 24 hours of preparation and was not observed to be date marked: KIMCHI, CUT CABBAGE, COOKED CHICKEN, COOKED POTATO NOODLES
violations.corrective_action: Refrigerated, ready-to-eat, time/temperature control for safety foods that are prepared on site and kept for more than 24 hours cannot have a shelf-life of more than 7 days, including the day of preparation. These food items must be marked with either the 'consume-by' date and/or 'preparation' date, color-coded labels, or another marking system/method that effectively indicates shelf-life that is clearly understood and properly used by the employees. CDI: PIC ORDERED DATE MARK STICKERS AND BEGAN PUTTING DATES ON ITEMS DURING INSPECTION.

out_items.name: Time as a Public Health Control; procedures and records

violations.title: TPHC, Food Marked with 4 Hour End Point
violations.observation: The following food item(s) for which time rather than temperature is used as a control is not marked or otherwise identified to indicate the time that is 4 hours past the point in time when the food is removed from temperature control: KIMCHI, PICKLED RADISH
violations.corrective_action: If time only, rather than time in accordance with temperature control, up to a maximum of 4 hours, is used as the public health control the food shall: 1) have an initial temperature of 41F or less if removed from cold holding temperature OR 135F or above if removed from hot holding temperature control, 2) be marked or otherwise identified to indicate the time that is 4 hours past the point in time when the food is removed from temperature control, 3) be cooked and served, served if ready-to-eat, or discarded within 4 hours from the point in time when the food is removed from temperature control, and 4) be discarded if unmarked or marked to exceed a 4 hour limit. CDI: END TIME ADDED TO FOOD CONTAINERS ON TPHC. PIC RE-EDUCATED.

out_items.name: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used

violations.title: Restriction & Storage; Medicines Location
violations.observation: Employees' medicines are not properly located to prevent contamination of food and food contact surfaces. OBSERVED EMPLOYEE MEDICINE STORED WITH TO GO CONTAINERS ON THE PREP-LINE.
violations.corrective_action: Employees' medicines shall be properly stored to prevent contamination of food and food contact surfaces. CDI: MEDICINE MOVED DURING INSPECTION. PIC RE-EDUCATED.

violations.title: Food Storage Container, Common Name
violations.observation: The following food items that are not easily identified by appearance were observed without a label: SQUEEZE BOTTLES OF OILS AND SAUCES AT THE COOKLINE.
violations.corrective_action: Unless a food item can be easily recognized, all foods and ingredients removed from their original containers and stored in working containers shall be labeled using the common name of the food. For example: cooking oils, salt, sugar, flour, spices, herbs, etc. LABEL ALL WORKING CONTAINERS OF FOOD. ENSURE THIS IS CORRECTED BY YOUR NEXT ROUTINE INSPECTION.

out_items.name: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage, and display

violations.title: Food Storage 6 inches above Floor
violations.observation: Food stored on the floor and/or food stored less than 6 inches off the floor. OBSERVED POP STORED ON THE FLOOR BEHIND THE CASH REGISTER/SERVING AREA.
violations.corrective_action: Food shall be protected from contamination by storing the food at least 6 inches off the floor on approved shelving units or dunnage racks. Milk crates, soda crates, or bread racks are not suitable for food storage. ENSURE ALL DRINKS ARE STORED 6IN ABOVE THE FLOOR BY YOUR NEXT ROUTINE INSPECTION.

violations.title: In-Use Utensils Proper Storage
violations.observation: Dispensing and/or in-use utensils improperly stored between use as follows: OBSERVED IN TWO-DOOR PREP-TOP COOLER: TONGS FOR THE RAW BEEF WERE COVERED IN RAW BEEF WITH THE HANDLE LAYING IN THE BEEF.
violations.corrective_action: During pauses in food preparation or dispensing, food utensils shall be stored in one of the following manners: 1) in the food with their handles above the top of the food and the container, 2) in food that is not time/temperature control for safety (TCS) food with their handles above the top of the food within containers or equipment that can be closed, 3) on a clean portion of the food preparation table or cooking equipment only if the in-use utensil and the food contact surface of the food preparation table or cooking equipment are cleaned and sanitized, 4) in running water of sufficient velocity to flush particulates to the drain, 5) in a clean, protected location if the utensils are used only with a food that is NOT TCS food, or 6) in a container of water if the water is maintained at a temperature of at least 135F and the container is cleaned frequently. CDI: TONGS REMOVED. PIC RE-EDUCATED. Dolpan (Inspection Date: 07/22/2026) Page 3 of 4

out_items.name: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used

violations.title: Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, Durable/Smooth Materials
violations.observation: The nonfood-contact surface of the following equipment is not corrosion resistant, nonabsorbent, and/or smooth: OBSERVED FOIL LINING SHELVING IN THE KITCHEN.
violations.corrective_action: Non-food contact surfaces of equipment that are exposed to splash, spillage, or other foods that require frequent cleaning shall be constructed of a corrosion- resistant, nonabsorbent, and smooth material. ALL FOIL AND CARDBOARD MUST BE REMOVED FROM THE SHELVING BY YOUR NEXT ROUTINE INSPECTION. YOU MUST PAINT OVER THE RUST SPOTS ON THE SHELVING OR REPLACE THEM. RETRAIN EMPLOYEES TO CEASE USING FOIL AND CARDBOARD TO AVOID CLEANING.

out_items.name: Consumer advisory provided for raw and undercooked food

violations.title: Consumer Advisory for Raw/Undercooked Food, Disclosure
violations.observation: The following raw and/or undercooked foods are provided on the menu, menu board, table tent or brochure without proper disclosure: OBSERVED MULTIPLE DISHES INCLUDING BULGOGI REQUIRING AN ASTERISK ON THE MENU ON THE WALL AND ON THE COUNTER.
violations.corrective_action: The Consumer Advisory shall include a disclosure statement that includes a description of the animal-derived foods as raw/undercooked or identification of the animal-derived foods by asterisking (*) them to a footnote that states that the items are served raw or undercooked, or contain raw or undercooked ingredients. CDI: PIC BEGAN PRINTING OUT STARS AND STUCK THEM TO THE MENU DURING THE INSPECTION. PLEASE SEND THE REDONE MENU TO ME BEFORE YOU PURCHASE IT.

out_items.name: Consumer advisory provided for raw and undercooked food

violations.title: Consumer Advisory for Raw/Undercooked Food
violations.observation: A review of the menu with the foodservice operator indicates that there is no consumer advisory for the following food item(s) that may be served raw and/or undercooked: fried sunny side up egg on the menu did not have a consumer advisory
violations.corrective_action: If an animal food such as beef, eggs, fish, lamb, milk, pork, poultry, or shellfish is served or sold raw or undercooked the permit holder shall inform consumers of the significantly increased risk of consuming such foods by way of a disclosure and reminder using brochures, deli case or menu advisories, label statements, table tents, placards, or other effective written means. Language for consumer advisory was provided to PIC, PIC printed signs for the sunny side up eggs

violations.observation: Dispensing and/or in-use utensils improperly stored between use as follows: observed in use knife and knife sharpener being stored in between two under counter cooler in such a manner that the food contact surface is not being stored in a sanitary manner
violations.corrective_action: During pauses in food preparation or dispensing, food utensils shall be stored in one of the following manners: 1) in the food with their handles above the top of the food and the container, 2) in food that is not time/temperature control for safety (TCS) food with their handles above the top of the food within containers or equipment that can be closed, 3) on a clean portion of the food preparation table or cooking equipment only if the in-use utensil and the food contact surface of the food preparation table or cooking equipment are cleaned and sanitized, 4) in running water of sufficient velocity to flush particulates to the drain, 5) in a clean, protected location if the utensils are used only with a food that is NOT TCS food, or 6) in a container of water if the water is maintained at a temperature of at least 135F and the container is cleaned frequently PIC removed knife and utensil so it was being stored in a a sanitary manner
